title: KV cache phase-diagram benchmark: mapping hit-rate, memory pressure, and p95 behavior
creator: Maya Patel
description: This ticket builds a reproducible phase-diagram style benchmark that characterizes KV/prefix cache behavior across three axes: effective hit rate, memory allocation budget, and p95 token latency (and tokens/sec). The goal is to identify phase boundaries where latency or throughput collapses under memory pressure or skew changes, and to encode those boundaries into automated regression detection jobs.
hypothesis: A small change in eviction policy or kernel scheduling can move the system from a 'graceful degradation' region into a 'collapse' region with sharp p95 increases. These boundaries are stable across seeds for realistic workload families (Zipf alpha 0.8-1.2) but differ significantly when sequence-length distributions shift (chatty vs. short prompts).
experiment_design: Cross-factor grid over: hotset fraction (0.1% - 20%), Zipf alpha (0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2), memory budget percent (10%, 25%, 50%, 75% of baseline), and sequence-length profile (short/medium/long).
Runs at three concurrency levels to expose batching effects: 50, 300, 1200 tok/s target per GPU instance using our load-generator.

Collect per-run metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies (generation time), tokens/sec, tail CPU/GPU utilization, memory RSS, eviction rate, prefix-cache hit-rate, KV lookup latency distribution, and GC/allocator churn.
Repeat each cell with 5 different random seeds and synthetic hotkey permutations to estimate variance and false-positive regression rate.
matrix: Seq-length profiles: short (mean 32 tokens), medium (mean 128), long (mean 512)
Concurrency targets: low (50 tok/s/gpu), medium (300 tok/s/gpu), high (1200 tok/s/gpu)
threshold_alerting: Alert if p95 increases > 2x relative to baseline for same cell
Alert if tokens/sec drops > 30% while hit-rate > 50% (indicates non-cache-related regression)
Alert on sudden increase in eviction rate > 5x baseline
Regression detector: combine EWMA on p95 with CUSUM on tokens/sec; raise tentative alert when both signals exceed thresholds for 3/5 seeds
infra_requirements: Dedicated benchmark cluster with 4x identical GPU instances (same kernel/driver) to run parallel grid cells
Instrumented runtime build: bench-mode metrics enabled (kv telemetry, detailed latency histograms)
runbook: Step 1: Provision benchmark cluster via infra/bench-playbook (use pool 'phase-diagram-staging').
Step 2: Deploy runtime image tagged 'bench/phase-2026-03-01' with verbose kv telemetry enabled.
Step 3: Kick off param sweep using bench-loadgen orchestration script (bench/orchestrate_phase_sweep.sh).
Step 4: Monitor Grafana for runaway p95 or memory thrash; if observed, abort cell and mark as 'collapse' region.
Step 5: Collect artifacts (logs, histograms, heap dumps) into S3; attach links to this ticket and update results_summary.
results_summary: Initial runs (first 72 cells) show a clear knee where p95 jumps nonlinearly as memory budget drops below ~25% for hotset fractions >=1% with Zipf alpha >=1.0. Long-sequence workloads shift the knee to higher memory budgets. EWMA+CUSUM detection reduced false positives from 18% to 6% in our seeded repeats. Notable finding: our LRU+segmented-allocator variant exhibited a 2.3x higher eviction rate under high-concurrency bursts, moving multiple cells from 'graceful' to 'collapse' region.
next_steps: Expand the grid to include a tuned TTL eviction policy and a new 'adaptive-prefetch' feature flag to see if the phase boundary improves.
Integrate the phase-diagram job into nightly regression suite for runtime-1.20 with automatic triage labels when a new 'collapse' region appears.
Create a short PRD for potential runtime mitigations (prefetch heuristics, small-LLM resident caching) and share with PM and Design for prioritization.
Add a lightweight summary visualization (SVG) exported to Confluence for the on-call runbook.
